## In the Rāsa-pañcādhyāyī

- **The gopī Kṛṣṇa took away** (10.30.28, p. 229): «This fortunate *ramaṇī* has certainly worshiped Bhagavān Śrī Hari perfectly…» Viśvanātha: «*Rādhayati iti rādhā* — the use of the verbal root *rādh* denotes the name of this *ramaṇī* as Rādhā.»
- **«I cannot walk any further»** (10.30.38–40): proud of her fortune She said, «Take Me wherever Your mind desires»; Kṛṣṇa said «Climb on My shoulder» and vanished, and She lamented: «O lord, O lover, O dearest one, where are You?… I am Your most fallen maidservant.» Viśvanātha: She had only wished Him to rest, but «the potency that fills the *līlās* with loving sentiments covered Their ability to know each other's intentions».
- **The frowning gopī** (10.32.6): «Some other gopī, completely agitated from the anger of love, had raised her eyebrows and was biting her lips…» — Viśvanātha: her mood is *madīyatā* («Kṛṣṇa is mine!») with honey-like affection; «She is Śrīmatī Rādhā».
- The seven gopīs: Kṛṣṇa reappeared in the rāsa (*Bhāgavatam* 10.32.4–8), «In the five verses beginning with *kācit*, Śukadeva Gosvāmī describes the different moods of some of the prominent *vraja-devīs*» (Jīva Gosvāmī's *Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī*). Viśvanātha Cakravartī's *Sārārtha-darśinī* names them: the gopī who took His right hand in her joined palms is **Candrāvalī**; the one who put His left arm on her shoulder, **Śyāmalā**; the one who took His chewed betel, **Śaibyā**; the one who placed His foot on her breast, **Padmā**; the one who frowned and bit her lips, **Śrī Rādhā**; the one who drank His face with unblinking eyes, **Lalitā**; the one who took Him into her heart through her eyes and closed them «like a yogī», **Viśākhā**. «The *Śrī Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī* describes these seven confidantes… Candrāvalī, Śyāmalā, Śaibyā, Padmā, Śrī Rādhā, Lalitā and Viśākhā», and the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa* gives the eighth, **Bhadrā** (pp. 337–354).
- Of all the gopīs «Kṛṣṇa's topmost beloved is Śrī Rādhā… Only Śrī Rādhā is Rāseśvarī, the mistress of the circle dance» (introduction); «out of these eight cowherd damsels, Śrī Rādhā is the most prominent» (p. 354).
- In the *Skanda Purāṇa* (Dvārakā-māhātmya of the *Prahlāda-saṁhitā*), when Uddhava came again to Vraja and met the gopīs at Māyā-sarovara, eight of them spoke; Rādhā said: «The one who never felt fear of sin in killing Pūtanā, O sakhīs, will surely kill any woman. Is there any doubt about this?» (quoted p. 348–349).

Source: *Śrī Rāsa-pañcādhyāyī* (Bhāgavatam 10.29–33 with the commentaries of Śrīdhara Svāmī, Jīva Gosvāmī and Viśvanātha Cakravartī; ed. Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī).
